clue.text: Swimmer hit, intercepted by men on board boat

indicators.note: something intercepted is cut into midway, so the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: to bash is to hit hard
kings are pieces (men) on a chess or draughts board
an ark is a boat, as Noah's was

explanation.surface: A swimmer is struck while sailors on a boat look on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men on board' suggests sailors, but here it means pieces on a chessboard, and 'Swimmer' is a fish, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The basking shark is a huge plankton-eating fish, so it is literally a swimmer.

clue.text: Drunk smart to follow after vehicle turned up

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the first in the answer
in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle, a taxi
chic means smart or stylish

explanation.surface: A tipsy dandy follows a car that has rolled over.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'turned up' means reading from the bottom, which reverses the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchic, after Bacchus the wine god, describes drunken revelry, so it can mean drunk.

clue.text: Good person on carriage is one in flight

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on top of the next comes first

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person
carriage in the sense of bearing or manner, an air

explanation.surface: A virtuous passenger sits in a carriage, perhaps one of a pair travelling together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in flight' sounds like an air passenger, but a flight is a run of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps is made of single stairs, so each step is one member of the flight.

clue.text: Being overturned, declare bill is partly prejudiced

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the letters run upwards, so they are read in reverse
only part of the words declare bill is is used, the answer sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A government overruled wants to announce that a bill is biased.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'declare bill is' backwards gives SILLIBERALCED; the answer sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiberal means narrow-minded and intolerant, which is close to being biased or bigoted.

clue.text: Become pregnant

definitions.meaning: ... as a past participle can mean become, as in 'has ... grey' for 'has become grey'
... means pregnant for a stated time, as in 'six months ...'

explanation.surface: An instruction to conceive a child.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, but it splits into two separate senses of the same short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idiomatic: 'gone quiet' means turned quiet, and 'she is five months gone' means expecting.

clue.text: Uncaring ambassador put on eastern robe after changing sides

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: right is swapped for left, R and L being the abbreviations for the two sides

parts.note: to robe is to dress

explanation.surface: An indifferent diplomat dons oriental clothing after switching allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after changing sides' wants to mean defecting; here it swaps right (R) for left (L) in the robe word.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedless means paying no attention, careless of consequences, so close to uncaring.

clue.text: Not opening, toy gun

indicators.note: the word is used without its opening letter

parts.note: to toy with is to trifle

explanation.surface: A toy gun that won't open for loading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toy' looks like an adjective for 'gun' but is the verb trifle; 'Not opening' removes its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm, a kind of gun.

clue.text: Unusually, Vatican City needing no prison industry

indicators.note: used unusually, the letters are put into an odd order
the letters of the named piece are left out of the mix

parts.note: can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Remarkably, the Vatican has no jail of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking C, A and N from VATICAN CITY leaves VATICITY, and 'Unusually' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry in the sense of busy effort or diligence is close to activity, lively doing.

clue.text: Definitely tell when Frenchman's very upset

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so read backwards

parts.note: très is French for very

explanation.surface: Saying something firmly because a Frenchman is very distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns TRES into SERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert is to state forcefully and with confidence, so to tell definitely.

clue.text: Church claim to collect new tax

indicators.note: the claim takes in the next piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: to allege is to claim

explanation.surface: A church announces it will gather a fresh levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax' looks like a noun, a levy, but is the verb meaning to test or strain.
explanation.definitionFit: To tax someone is to make demands on them, to test them, which is to challenge.

clue.text: Home in France destructive creature stripped

parts.note: F is the international code for France

indicators.note: stripped of its outer layer, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a locust devours crops

explanation.surface: A French house where a pest has eaten everything bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home in France' looks like one phrase; 'Home in' is the definition. 'stripped' takes L and T from LOCUST.
explanation.definitionFit: To focus on something is to concentrate attention on it, which is to home in on it.

clue.text: Reportedly pick up purchase with this

indicators.note: the phrase is as it would be spoken, giving a word that matches it in speech

parts.note: pick up means hear, and purchase means buy

explanation.surface: Someone said to collect a bought item using this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick up' means collect in the surface but hear in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereby is a formal word meaning by means of this, as in 'I hereby declare'.

clue.text: Part of organ having infection, spot in peer's heart

parts.note: flu is an infection

indicators.note: the spot is placed inside the next piece
the heart of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: a pip is a spot, as on dice or cards

explanation.surface: An organ, perhaps a nobleman's heart, has an infection and a blemish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' gives EE from the middle of PEER; PIP goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A flue pipe is one of the pipes of a church organ that sounds like a whistle, without a reed.

clue.text: Scullery-maid casually cutting last bit of lemon for drinks

indicators.note: the letter is cut out of the name

parts.note: Cinders is the casual name for Cinderella, the scullery-maid of the pantomime

indicators.note: the final letter of the word lemon

explanation.surface: A kitchen maid offhandedly slices lemon for some drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The N at the end of 'lemon' is cut from CINDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciders are alcoholic drinks made from fermented apples.

clue.text: Did adopting the Euro make Germans so limited?

definitions.text: Did adopting the Euro make Germans so limited?

parts.words: Did adopting the Euro make Germans so limited?
parts.note: Germany swapped its Deutschmark for the euro, so Germans were left without their mark; the clue also asks for a word meaning bounded

explanation.surface: A question whether the single currency cramped Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The Deutschmark was Germany's currency before the euro, so Germans were left without the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To demark is to mark the limits of something, so demarked means bounded or limited.

clue.text: Dreamer ordered spacesuit, ditching uniform

indicators.note: ordered here means placed in a new order, so the letters are rearranged
ditching means getting rid of, so these letters are left out of the mix

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dreamer bought a spacesuit without the rest of the uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditching' drops U from SPACESUIT, and 'ordered' rearranges SPACESIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapist seeks refuge from reality in fantasy, a daydreamer.

clue.text: Hand woman blouse — being totally uncovered is irregular

indicators.note: each word is uncovered, losing its outer letters at both ends

explanation.surface: A woman is handed a blouse; going about nude would be unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being totally uncovered' takes the outside letters from Hand, woman and blouse, leaving AN, OMA and LOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Anomalous means departing from the norm, so it is a synonym for irregular.

clue.text: Model makers cut each minute tree

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Hornby is a British maker of model railways

explanation.surface: Model makers chop down a tiny tree.
explanation.walkthrough: HORNBY is the famous British toy-train company; 'cut' drops its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornbeam is a hardwood tree common in European hedges and woodland.

clue.text: Play that's funny by epic writer

parts.note: ha is a laugh, said at something funny
John Milton wrote the epic poem Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: A comic play is written by an epic poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' is fair because Hamilton is a hit stage musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamilton is Lin-Manuel Miranda's musical about Alexander Hamilton, a stage show.

clue.text: Respect journal article for gardening circles

indicators.note: circles means surrounds, so this piece goes round the other

parts.note: to hoe is to do gardening with a hoe
a mag, short for magazine, is a journal

explanation.surface: Praise for a magazine piece written for gardening clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circles' looks like a noun, as in clubs, but is the verb surround.
explanation.definitionFit: Homage is public respect or honour paid to someone.

clue.text: Ingratiate oneself backing society with informal agreement

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: yup is a casual yes

explanation.surface: Someone supporting a club tries to curry favour with a casual yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' wants to mean supporting; it reverses SOC.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosy up to someone is an idiom for getting close to them to win favour.

clue.text: Warning after blending Iberian wines

indicators.note: blended, the two words merge and share one letter where they meet

parts.note: port is Portuguese wine and tent is a Spanish red wine

explanation.surface: A cautionary note after mixing Spanish and Portuguese wines.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT and TENT 'blending' overlap so the shared T appears once. TENT is an old name for a dark red Spanish wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is an omen of something coming, often bad, so a warning.

clue.text: Batter around second-rate fish showing veiny appearance

indicators.note: turned around, the word is read backwards

parts.note: to ram is to batter
B grade means second-rate
a ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Battering a poor-quality fish to cook it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batter' looks like the cooking coating but is the verb ram; 'around' turns it to MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Marbling is a streaked pattern like marble, as in veined meat or paper.

clue.text: Vessel capsized on duck

indicators.note: capsized means turned upside down, so in a down clue the letters are read backwards

parts.note: re means on or about
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, nil

explanation.surface: A boat has overturned onto a waterbird.
explanation.walkthrough: RENIL is reversed by 'capsized'.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship, a vessel.

clue.text: Stray is pale with colour coming back

parts.note: wan means pale

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: A pale stray regains its colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stray' looks like a noun, a lost animal, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander is to roam off course, which is to stray.

clue.text: Thrust plunger with water ultimately rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letter moves upwards, nearer the start

parts.note: a diver plunges into water

indicators.note: the final letter of water

explanation.surface: A plunger pushes down as the water finally rises.
explanation.walkthrough: The R that ends 'water' also ends DIVER; 'rising' moves it up two places.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive as a noun means a forceful push or energetic urge, a thrust.

clue.text: Bad reaction from alcohol, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals the word as spoken, matched by a different spelling

parts.note: booze is slang for alcohol

explanation.surface: Drinking too much is said to cause a bad reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad reaction' looks like a hangover; it is an audience's response.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience boos to show disapproval, an unfavourable response to a show.

clue.text: On which people are putting young

definitions.meaning: a putting ... in golf is where players putt

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a place where people put the youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' reads as placing, but it is the golf stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf putts are played on the green, and a green recruit is a young novice.

clue.text: English player Paul regularly coached about budget

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: Paul Simon is a musician, a player

indicators.note: every other letter of the word coached is taken

explanation.surface: An English footballer called Paul trained steadily about money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes OCE from coached; ESIMONOCE is then turned 'about'. 'English player' reads like a footballer, but the player is musician Paul Simon.
explanation.definitionFit: To budget is to plan spending carefully, so as a verb it means to economise.

clue.text: Likely culprit with pies and crumpets going walkabout

indicators.note: going walkabout means wandering off, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: The prime suspect is whoever made off with the pies and crumpets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going walkabout' is the anagram signal for PIES plus CRUMPETS.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime suspect is the person police most suspect, the most likely culprit.
